candidates.tier_reason: Two refereed papers attribute it to the star: Robertson et al. 2015 (48.6 d = Prot/3 with Prot 143 d) and Bortle et al. 2021 (GP with Prot 125 d; adding a planet does not help; 'both previously reported planets are artifacts of the star's rotation and activity'). A homogeneous HARPS-only reanalysis (Mignon et al. 2024, 228 RVs) fits a constant. Only the discoverers' rebuttal (arXiv:1506.09072) and Tuomi et al. 2019 (unrefereed) keep it alive. Contested rather than formally retracted, so recorded here as unlikely; the writer may prefer to treat it as refuted.
candidates.orbit_flags: RV only (HARPS + HIRES + PFS). K = 2.25 +/- 0.31 m/s, P, e, Msini and a from Anglada-Escude+2014 Table 2 (68% intervals). Period sits at ~Prot/3 (Robertson+2015, Prot 143 d) and is attributed to rotation by Bortle+2021 (Prot 125 d). Not seen in HARPS-only data (Mignon+2024). No inclination.
candidates.reference: Anglada-Escude et al. 2014, MNRAS 443, L89, 'Two planets around Kapteyn's star: a cold and a temperate super-Earth orbiting the nearest halo red dwarf', Table 2; disputed by Robertson et al. 2015, ApJL 805, L22 and Bortle et al. 2021, AJ 161, 230

incidental_finds_outside_my_scope.detail: Bortle et al. 2021 (AJ 161, 230; arXiv:2103.02709) conclude both Kapteyn b and c are rotation/activity artefacts (Prot 125 d vs P_c 121.5 d); Robertson et al. 2015 said c needs more data because it lies near Prot; Mignon et al. 2024 fit the 228 HARPS RVs of GJ 191 with a constant. exoplanet.eu marks both 'Controversial'. NASA pscomppars still lists Kapteyn c. Writer's judgement whether c stays on the confirmed tab.
